name: Thrall
summary: Thrall now rules from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar, Warchief of the Horde and ruler of Durotar. Once a human slave raised as an arena fighter, he freed his people, restored their shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to a new homeland.

sections.title: From Slave to Shaman
sections.body: Thrall was born Go'el, son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka. Gul'dan's assassins murdered his parents when he was an infant, and human commander Aedelas Blackmoore found him and named him Thrall, meaning slave. At Durnholde Keep, Blackmoore raised him as an arena fighter and taught him human tactics. With help from his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped. The Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar guided him away from demonic corruption and taught him to master the elemental spirits. Thrall became the first orcish shaman of a new generation.

sections.title: The Mantle of the Warchief
sections.body: After the Second War, Thrall joined Orgrim Doomhammer to free the orcs languishing in Alliance internment camps. Doomhammer fell in battle and passed his black plate armor and mighty warhammer to Thrall, naming him Warchief. The mysterious Prophet Medivh brought prophetic visions, and Thrall led his people aboard captured human ships across the Great Sea. They reached Kalimdor and escaped the doom falling upon the Eastern Kingdoms.

sections.title: Forging the New Horde
sections.body: In Kalimdor, Thrall reshaped the Horde from a warmongering force into an alliance built on survival and honor. He rescued Vol'jin's Darkspear trolls and allied with Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren. With human and night elf forces, the coalition defeated the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal. Thrall then founded Durotar and its capital, Orgrimmar, named for his father and mentor. He keeps an uneasy peace with Jaina Proudmoore's Theramore while defending his fragile nation and weighing controversial alliances, including the Forsaken of Lordaeron.

faq.answer: Thrall leads the orcish people as Warchief of the Horde. Born Go'el of the Frostwolf clan, he was raised by humans as an enslaved gladiator, then broke free, learned shamanic ways, and led the orcs to Kalimdor, where they founded Orgrimmar.

faq.q: Where does Thrall's name come from?
faq.answer: Thrall was born Go'el, the name given by his parents Durotan and Draka. His human captor, Aedelas Blackmoore, gave him the name Thrall, an old human word meaning slave. Thrall kept it as a reminder of his past and of the oppression his people vowed never to endure again.

faq.q: Why does Thrall wear black armor and carry a hammer?
faq.answer: Thrall wears black plate armor and carries the Doomhammer, both passed to him by Orgrim Doomhammer, the former Warchief. Mortally wounded while freeing the orcs from the internment camps, Orgrim gave Thrall the weapon and the mantle of Warchief with his dying breath.

faq.q: Where can I find Thrall in the game?
faq.answer: Thrall resides in the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar, the Horde capital in Durotar. He stands inside Grommash Hold with his bodyguards and advisers.

faq.q: What is Thrall's relationship with Jaina Proudmoore?
faq.answer: Thrall and Lady Jaina Proudmoore earned mutual respect and forged a pact of cooperation while fighting together at Mount Hyjal during the Third War. Their factions remain deeply distrustful, but the two leaders work to preserve a fragile peace between Orgrimmar and Theramore.

faq.q: Why did Thrall allow the Forsaken into the Horde?
faq.answer: Though wary of the undead, Thrall recognized the desperate plight of Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, who had freed themselves from the Lich King's control. The tauren urged him diplomatically, believing the Forsaken could be redeemed. Thrall admitted them to the Horde to secure a strategic foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms.

angles.text: Thrall is your Warchief and supreme commander. He led the Horde out of enslavement and ruin toward an honorable future on Kalimdor.
Alliance leaders see Thrall as dangerous but pragmatic. His disciplined Horde is far preferable to the bloodthirsty conquerors of the First and Second Wars.
Thrall is revered as the first new orcish shaman in a generation. He restored his people's sacred communion with the elemental spirits after decades of demonic corruption.
To the orcs, Thrall is a living savior. He freed them from the lethargy of the human internment camps and returned them to their ancestral honor.
